newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA GOLD-Busang damage may hurt small miners.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA GOLD-Busang damage may hurt small miners.

text.p: Financing for the army of small and medium-sized gold companies in Australia may be in jeopardy in the wake of the Busang mining scandal in Indonesia, the World Gold Council (WGC) said on Tuesday.

"The junior mining companies, the principal source of new discoveries in Australia, could be facing difficulties in new financing now," George Milling-Stanley of the industry body's economic service told analysts.
A fall-out in financing outlets for the juniors would mean larger mining houses would be required to take up more early exploration projects, he said.
Less exploration by the juniors also poses a threat to Australia's ranking as the world's number three gold producer, Milling-Stanley said.
"This could have some implications for gold supplies," he said.

Busang, once touted as the richest gold find of the century, was found to be a massive fraud earlier this month. Bre-X Minerals Ltd stock subsequently collapsed, its shares were delisted from Canadian exchanges and Nasdaq and at least 10 lawsuits have been filed against the company.
Laurie Fitzgerald, resource research director for stock brokerage Hartley Poynton Ltd in Perth, home to many of Australia's small miners, agreed Busang was harmful.
Investment from Canada, where the fallout from Busang has been greatest, supply much of the financing for mine exploration in Australia, Fitzgerald said.
"There is no doubt the gold industry here has been tarnished by the activities of Busang," Fitzgerald said.
